security_spec.violation_condition: Under CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE, the kernel writes PMPCFG0 with L=0 RWX=111 (NAPOT allow-all) at head.S:240 assuming legacy PMP semantics; if firmware sets mseccfg.MML=1 before handoff (the expected Smepmp boot flow), this rule becomes S/U-mode-only per the Smepmp truth table (L=0 → enforced on S/U, denied in M), denying M-mode access to all memory. With mseccfg.MMWP also set, M-mode has no fallback allowlist, causing an immediate instruction fetch fault.
security_spec.summary: Kernel PMP init in head.S has zero Smepmp awareness: L=0 all-access rule becomes S/U-mode-only under MML=1, denying M-mode access and bricking the kernel when firmware has enabled Smepmp lockdown prior to handoff.

findings.finding: Under CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE, the kernel writes PMPCFG0 with L=0, RWX=111 (NAPOT allow-all) at lines 238–240 assuming legacy PMP semantics (M-mode always has unrestricted access to unlocked regions). If firmware has set mseccfg.MML=1 before handoff — the expected Smepmp boot flow per the 'Smepmp software discovery' spec section — the Smepmp truth table maps L=0,RWX=111 to 'Access Exception' in M-mode, denying M-mode all access to all memory (PMPADDR0=-1 covers the entire address space). With mseccfg.MMWP also set, M-mode has no fallback allowlist, causing an immediate instruction fetch fault on the very next instruction after the PMPCFG0 write. The kernel has zero Smepmp awareness: no mseccfg.MML check, no MML/MMWP/RLB bit definitions in csr.h (only PMM bits for Smmpm are defined), no 'smepmp' or 'Smepmp' string in any source file.
findings.snippet:
li a0, -1
csrw CSR_PMPADDR0, a0
li a0, (PMP_A_NAPOT | PMP_R | PMP_W | PMP_X)
csrw CSR_PMPCFG0, a0

findings.finding: csr.h defines only MSECCFG_PMM bit-fields (Smmpm pointer masking) but omits MML, MMWP, and RLB bit definitions required for Smepmp. Without these definitions, any kernel code that needs to check mseccfg.MML before writing PMP registers (as head.S:238–240 should) has no way to reference the field. This is the structural root cause of the Smepmp-blind PMP write in head.S.
findings.snippet:
/* mseccfg bits */
#define MSECCFG_PMM			ENVCFG_PMM
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16
